subsystems.name: Airframe
subsystems.role: a lightweight body that survives Titan's cold and the entry descent, and carries the science payload between landing sites.
parts: landing skids for the boggy surface

subsystems.name: Rotor system
subsystems.role: provides lift in Titan's dense, low-gravity atmosphere.
parts: eight rotors in four coaxial pairs

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: supplies electricity and waste heat for decades without sunlight, since Titan's haze blocks most solar power.
parts: radioisotope thermoelectric generator (the same type flown on Curiosity and Perseverance)

subsystems.name: Flight control and autonomy
subsystems.role: flies the hops without a pilot, because radio commands take more than an hour to arrive.

subsystems.name: Instruments
subsystems.role: characterises surface chemistry at each site, especially prebiotic organic molecules.
parts: mass spectrometer with gas chromatograph, derived from the SAM instrument on Curiosity

subsystems.name: Thermal system
parts: waste-heat routing from the power source

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: sends data back to Earth, either directly or via a relay.

buildSteps.title: Design the mission profile
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose the Selk crater region as the landing zone: a site where water ice and organic material may have mixed after an impact.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the airframe
buildSteps.detail: Carbon-fibre composite panels and spars are laid up and cured into a body light enough to fly but stiff enough to survive launch vibration.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the rotorcraft
buildSteps.detail: Four arms are fitted with coaxial rotor pairs — eight rotors in total — sized for an atmosphere about 1.5 times Earth's pressure and gravity about one-seventh as strong.

buildSteps.title: Install power and thermal hardware
buildSteps.detail: The radioisotope generator is mounted with its shielding, and insulation and heat paths are built around the electronics.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the instruments
buildSteps.detail: The mass spectrometer, gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer, meteorology package and cameras are installed and calibrated.

buildSteps.title: Test in a Titan-like chamber
buildSteps.detail: The lander is run in a cold, nitrogen-and-methane atmosphere at Titan pressure to prove the rotors, thermal control and instruments work there.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: Planned for launch in 2028, the craft flies a multi-year interplanetary trajectory to Saturn's moon, arriving around 2034.

buildSteps.title: Enter, descend and land
buildSteps.detail: A heat shield and parachute slow the descent through the thick atmosphere, then the rotors take over for the final powered landing.

buildSteps.title: Fly the science campaign
buildSteps.detail: On the ground it waits for a clear radio link, then hops several kilometres at a time to a new site — hundreds of kilometres over the mission.

prerequisites.why: Titan's haze means solar panels cannot supply enough power; plutonium-238 generators have flown on Mars rovers and outer-planet probes.
the long radio delay rules out joystick flying, so the vehicle must sense and avoid hazards on its own.
the NASA Deep Space Network provides the link from Saturn's distance.
identifying organic molecules at each site requires lab-grade instruments shrunk to a few kilograms.
sustained operation at around -180 °C is unusual for motors, lubricants and batteries and needs dedicated testing.

pathway.milestone: assembly and environmental testing of the flight vehicle, led by a NASA laboratory in Maryland
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the rotorcraft can fly and survive in Titan conditions.
a working deep-space rotorcraft, the first flying vehicle on another world.

pathway.milestone: landing and the baseline multi-year flight campaign across the crater region
pathway.unlocks: a map of surface organics across many sites rather than one spot.

pathway.milestone: successor Titan craft — balloons, lake landers or longer-range rotorcraft
pathway.unlocks: access to the moon's seas and polar terrain, and a template for aerial exploration of Mars or Venus.
